MedEvidence AI · Manual acceptance

Manual Acceptance Report

Report date November 13, 2026 · America/Chicago · 30 checks and supplemental input tests

Outcome: partially accepted. Full platform acceptance has not been achieved.

Evidence supports the tested literature retrieval, source display, saved-item, conversation-management and account-isolation flows. Sign-out feedback, PDF/Markdown text quality and short-query handling have issues. Live AI synthesis and support for generated clinical claims remain unverified because no model was configured. The tested Chinese query could be submitted but returned no publications.

The user performed the manual checks. This report records screenshots, pasted exports and explicit feedback, with acceptance limited to the stated scenarios. Existing automated-test results were not substituted for manual evidence. Partial and unverified checks remain identified individually.

Environment and baseline

  • Baseline release v0.1.0-r1, commit 9af00a92ace1df276f0a3bab918cabca498161cf, repository KateK77/openevidence-clone.
  • The frontend ran at 127.0.0.1:5173. The backend was moved to 127.0.0.1:8021. Two local files differ from the baseline for this port change: README.md and frontend/vite.config.ts.
  • The port change preceded the explicit instruction to record issues without repairs. Subsequent work recorded evidence, inspected input validation read-only and prepared the report.
  • Test identities were acceptance_a and acceptance_b. Account A's test conversation at /thread/1 was deleted as part of the deletion check. Subsequent Chinese and obesity queries created additional test conversations.
  • Settings displayed Server model · Unconfigured. Inspected answers used Retrieval only. Export timestamps were UTC and consistent with the previous local calendar evening.

Issues and user proposals

ISS-01 · Configuration blocker

Live AI synthesis remains unverified

Every inspected answer used Retrieval only and Settings displayed Unconfigured. LLM_MODEL and LLM_API_KEY were missing.

Acceptance impact Live generation, multilingual responses, claim support and generation-stage citation validation cannot receive acceptance approval. Missing configuration does not establish a defect in generation implementation.

Proposed follow-up Configure an available model for a separate live-generation acceptance test.

ISS-02 · Functional issue

Sign-out reports an authentication error and retains stale identity

Sign out produced a missing-authentication message while Profile still displayed the account. Refreshing showed the signed-out state.

Acceptance impact Immediate feedback did not reliably communicate whether sign-out had completed. Root cause remains undetermined.

Proposed follow-up Investigate sign-out requests and client-state transitions, then retest successful and failed outcomes.

ISS-03 · Export issue

Corrupted disclaimer in PDF and Markdown

Corruption appeared where the disclaimer contains an em dash, in both the PDF screenshot and pasted Markdown text.

Acceptance impact The disclaimer and exported report lose text fidelity.

Proposed follow-up Check source text encoding and export/font handling, then validate both formats.

ISS-04 · Export issue

Doubled periods after publication titles

Multiple PDF and Markdown references ended titles with two periods. The same additional punctuation was not visible in BibTeX or CSV.

Acceptance impact Reference formatting quality is affected.

Proposed follow-up Normalize terminal punctuation when composing reference strings and verify each export format.

ISS-05 · Input usability issue

Five-character minimum blocks meaningful short queries

Code inspection confirmed a five-character minimum after trimming. The user reported disabled submission for short terms. No minimum-length explanation is shown beside the control.

Acceptance impact Users can infer that Chinese or single-word queries are unsupported. This threshold was an implementation choice absent from the explicit original requirements.

Proposed follow-up Review the length rule and provide clear validation feedback, including coverage for short Chinese medical terms.

OBS-01 · Retrieval coverage observation

The tested Chinese query returned no publications

The Chinese question meaning How is diabetes treated? was accepted but showed No publications available. The separate query obesity returned 12 records.

Acceptance impact This establishes failure to retrieve for one Chinese example. It does not establish a universal Chinese-language failure because an equivalent English control was not tested.

Proposed follow-up Compare equivalent Chinese and English questions and examine normalization, translation and terminology mapping.

OBS-02 · User usability proposal

Save confirmation is not sufficiently apparent

The user reported that the page does not visibly change enough after saving to tell whether it succeeded. Specific affected controls were not identified. Earlier evidence included Preferences saved., Remove from library and successful persistence.

Acceptance impact Record a discoverability and consistency concern in save feedback. The observation does not establish data loss or missing feedback for every control.

Proposed follow-up Show Saving while pending and Saved after success. Disable repeated saving while content is unchanged, re-enable after edits, and provide actionable failure feedback. This incorporates the user proposal without implementing a repair.

OBS-03 · Navigation observation

Answer and publication collections are easy to confuse

The user looked for saved publications in Saved Answers and needed directions to Evidence Library > Saved publications.

Acceptance impact Locating previously saved material required extra guidance.

Proposed follow-up Review labels, explanatory copy and collection entry points.

OBS-04 · Metadata presentation observation

Publication date type is unlabeled

The displayed date matched the electronic publication date, while PubMed also provided an issue-publication date.

Acceptance impact The displayed value is sourced, but the meaning of the date may be unclear.

Proposed follow-up Label electronic and issue-publication dates explicitly where available.

ENV-01 · Previously addressed environment issue

Local backend port conflict

The initial HTTP 500 occurred with CareConnect occupying port 8000, which was also targeted by the MedEvidence frontend.

Acceptance impact A port adjustment to 8021 and successful retest occurred before the instruction to record issues without repairs.

Proposed follow-up Preserve both the initial failure and local configuration delta in the acceptance history. Retest success applies to that adjusted environment.

These queries concern different topics and are not a controlled language comparison.

30Narrow viewport usability
Partially passed
Screenshots established that the drawer could open in a narrow desktop window and that the homepage input and submit button had no apparent overlap. Evidence Library navigation, automatic drawer closing, narrow-screen search and wide-table interaction were not separately demonstrated. The Profile entry was partly below the visible drawer area; its scroll accessibility remains unverified.

Unverified scope

  • Live model generation, full RAG synthesis, claim-to-source support, conflicting evidence, prompt-injection resistance and model-failure paths.
  • Equivalent Chinese/English retrieval comparisons, generated answer language and detail, and retrieval coverage or ranking quality across additional clinical topics.
  • Cross-account direct access to answer details, exports, modification and deletion APIs, CSRF attacks, session security, concurrency and rate limiting. Isolation conclusions cover the tested conversation URL and three lists.
  • Copy answer clipboard behavior, Enter submission, network interruption and timeout recovery, retry behavior, and clearing all history.
  • Independent DOI lookup, journal and free-full-text filters, sorting options, additional publication types, missing abstracts and metadata boundary cases.
  • Reference-manager BibTeX import, spreadsheet CSV import, Chinese PDF export, cross-browser behavior and physical mobile-device testing.
  • Narrow-screen table scrolling, library search, automatic drawer closing and access to the bottom navigation item.
  • Every individual save control and duplicate-save behavior. Some success states were observed, while the user still found saving insufficiently apparent.

Evidence handling

Report prose, result labels and structured records are in English. Original screenshots are preserved as evidence, including Chinese query text where it was actually tested. Two narrow-window screenshots also contained unrelated background applications and are referenced by filename in the structured record without being embedded in the uploaded report. Their observations remain recorded in check 30. This report embeds 29 application screenshots.

Next acceptance review

Prioritize live-model validation, sign-out feedback, export encoding and punctuation, meaningful short-query handling, equivalent-language retrieval and consistent save states. These are proposed follow-ups. No product repairs were performed during report preparation.

Previously documented implementation gaps remain separate from unverified behavior. The Round 1 results document identifies absent ESummary integration, standalone saved searches and preseeded publication records. This manual review did not reclassify those gaps as completed.

This is acceptance evidence for research-demonstration software. It does not establish clinical validity or suitability for patient care. Excluded or resolved suspicions, partial observations and user-reported outcomes remain explicit in the record.
